source.title: Information-Theoretic Probing with Minimum Description Length
source.venue: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)

confidence_rationale: Voita and Titov replace probe accuracy with the MDL of transmitting labels given representations (variational and online codes). The code length counts both the data given the probe and the effort of learning the probe, so a powerful probe cannot hide the work of extraction. This is a working example of GOV-CONTRACT-3's relocation rule: a claim that information is 'there' must pay for the decoder that finds it. Held at 0.5 because it concerns probes on language-model representations, a different setting, and MDL still depends on the chosen probe family and coding scheme.
failure_signatures: Description length depends on probe architecture and coding scheme; different choices can reorder which representation looks more 'informative'.
Probing measures decodability by an external reader, not use by the actual downstream consumer (INV-105's rung distinction).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Probe accuracy fails to separate representations from random or control baselines because a powerful probe can learn the task itself; measuring the minimum description length of labels given representations (which counts both data fit and the effort to reach it) gives stable, more informative comparisons.
mapping.ree_translation: GOV-CONTRACT-3 refuses a reduction when the lost distinctions reappear in 'a more powerful decoder'. MDL probing is a measurement procedure that charges for decoder effort in bits, so it is a candidate operationalisation of cost terms 'information rate + decoder complexity' under a two-part / online code.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The setting is external linguistic probes on pretrained transformers, not REE module-to-module handoffs. It shows the method is practical and that ignoring decoder cost gives misleading answers; it does not show REE's contract cost is estimable at the precision needed (a falsifying branch of the rule).
mapping.source_context: NLP interpretability paper building on the MDL principle (Rissanen; see Grunwald 2004 tutorial, arXiv math/0406077).

confidence_components.notes: Metadata (EMNLP 2020, pp. 183-196, DOI) from WebSearch hits of the ACL Anthology page; page itself not fetched (egress). Chosen over citing Grunwald's MDL tutorial alone because it applies MDL to exactly the decoder-power loophole.
